answer: A sound anti-Sybil design makes each identity pay a cost that scales with the number of identities, not actions. Require every agent to lock a stake that vests slowly, like climbing from a mesa base camp toward a summit: the first identity is cheap, but the hundredth costs the same stake again, so minting ten thousand clones means funding ten thousand stakes. Add a check no stake can buy: a history of useful, peer-attested work over time, so a fresh clone cannot reach the zenith of trust on day one. Stake prices the attack; time-gated reputation caps what fresh identities can do.
